family_rule: Every inferential test bearing on the risk-evidence relationship and on the design-confound diagnosis. Exclusions and their reasons are documented in the module docstring of src/12_multiplicity.py. A wider family adding construct validity, the in-scope subset re-runs and the adjudication-item associations is reported alongside, because the family definition is the only discretionary choice here and widening it makes the correction harder, not easier.

primary_family.family: primary: tests bearing on the risk-evidence relationship and its design confound

tests.label: H1 pooled: Spearman, risk tier ~ normalized evidence
tests.in_family_because: The primary association. If any test belongs in the family, this one does.

tests.label: H1 pooled: Kruskal-Wallis, evidence across the four tiers
tests.in_family_because: The second pre-specified test of the same hypothesis; the manuscript reports its p.

tests.label: Spearman, risk tier ~ interventional design
tests.in_family_because: Establishes 'tier is a design proxy', which is half the confound argument.

tests.label: Mann-Whitney, evidence by study design
tests.in_family_because: Establishes that evidence also differs by design, the other half of the confound argument.

tests.label: Spearman, tier ~ evidence within interventional studies
tests.in_family_because: The stratum the pre-specified estimator was written for; its CI excluding zero is a reported claim.

tests.label: Spearman, tier ~ evidence within observational studies
tests.in_family_because: The companion stratum, reported in the same sentence and on the same footing.

tests.label: Spearman, normalized evidence ~ log10 record length
tests.in_family_because: The manuscript claims record length does predict evidence; that is an inferential claim.

tests.label: Spearman, risk tier ~ log10 record length
tests.in_family_because: The manuscript claims length barely predicts tier, which is what makes length a weak confounder.
